claims.claim: Payments Canada owns and operates Lynx and ACSS; settlement uses Bank of Canada accounts.
RTR in sequenced Q4 2026 target launch; not confirmed live as of Oct 30.
Interac does not hold e-Transfer customer balances; financial institutions handle the bank accounts.
Interac shareholder types include banks, credit unions, caisses populaires and payment acquirers.
BCB owns Pix scheme and operates SPI and DICT.
SPI direct participants hold PI accounts at BCB; indirect participants settle through direct participant or special agent.
RTP participation does not require The Clearing House ownership or membership.
CHIPS uses a liquidity-saving mechanism to offset payment obligations and provides continuous settlement finality.
Eligible FCA-authorised non-bank PSPs can hold BoE settlement accounts subject to criteria; separate from reserves accounts.

CHIPS payments settle against the CHIPS Prefunded Balance Account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, held for the joint benefit of funding participants; TCH operates CHIPS and instructs the account as their agent and does not own the balances.

RTP settlement is final when the RTP system records the change in participants' positions, which are backed by a prefunded balance account at a Federal Reserve Bank funded through Fedwire or LMT; TCH is agent for funding participants and funding agents. The 2026 rules do not name the Reserve Bank; TCH's 2020 settlement note names FRBNY.

For USDC, Circle issues the token; the majority of reserves sit in the Circle Reserve Fund, a government money market fund managed by BlackRock, with The Bank of New York Mellon as fund custodian; the rest is cash at banks. Not a model for all stablecoins.
claims.source_date: Circle reserves as of 2026-10-26; N-CSR period ended 2025-10-31
